text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Prime minister Paavo Lipponen says rejected government proposal to liberalise retail stores' opening will be presented to parliament again as an issue of confidence in February.
- Women convicted of murder get lighter sentences than their male counterparts, survey shows.
- Finland has to clarify its position on Nato membership early next year, security expert says.

- Finnish Broadcasting Company YLE plans to sell its 11 percent stake in Finnish commercial television operator MTV Oy. MTV owners would be prepared to remove a paragraph in the bylaws that caps voting control at five percent.
- Den Danske Bank's planned Helsinki dealing room to be led by Tolten Bedretdin, now head of Dow Jones Telerate Finland.
- New Finnish national grid company has been actively contacted by potential financers from Finland and abroad. The company will have assets of almost seven billion markka.
- Tens of thousands of companies will next year be able to take rivalling bids for electricity supply when a 500 kilowatt effect limit is removed.

- The market for household equipment and white goods has grown by more than a third this year. A quarter of households now have a mobile phone and personal computers are almost as common, Statistics Finland survey shows.
- Industry-owned Olikluoto nuclear plant will this year reach its best-ever output -- 11.8 billion kilowatt hours.
- Mr Finland Kim Lofgren lost his title and got a one year and eight months prison sentence for several crimes of fraud.
- Agricultural support from the EU skews Finnish agriculture, research shows.
